From 96be65d12d792b3e177505db1225e1ec4f9cf5cd Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Wei Yongjun <weiyongjun1@huawei.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Feb 2019 09:18:41 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] gpio: tqmx86: Drop unnecessary gpiochip_remove in
 tqmx86_gpio_probe()

It's not necessary to remove gpio_chip which added with
devm_gpiochip_add_data().

Fixes: b868db94a6a7 ("gpio: tqmx86: Add GPIO from for this IO controller")
Signed-off-by: Wei Yongjun <weiyongjun1@huawei.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Lunn <andrew@lunn.ch>
Signed-off-by: Linus Walleij <linus.walleij@linaro.org>

diff --git a/drivers/gpio/gpio-tqmx86.c b/drivers/gpio/gpio-tqmx86.c
index 6f7250c6f597..33dbe483f92f 100644
--- a/drivers/gpio/gpio-tqmx86.c
+++ b/drivers/gpio/gpio-tqmx86.c
@@ -291,7 +291,7 @@ static int tqmx86_gpio_probe(struct platform_device *pdev)
 					   IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_BOTH);
 		if (ret) {
 			dev_err(dev, "Could not add irq chip\n");
-			goto out_remove;
+			goto out_pm_dis;
 		}
 
 		gpiochip_set_chained_irqchip(chip, irq_chip,
@@ -309,8 +309,6 @@ static int tqmx86_gpio_probe(struct platform_device *pdev)
 
 	return 0;
 
-out_remove:
-	gpiochip_remove(&gpio->chip);
 out_pm_dis:
 	pm_runtime_disable(&pdev->dev);
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/gpio/gpio-tqmx86.c`**
- The line that called `gpiochip_remove(&gpio->chip);` has been removed from the `tqmx86_gpio_probe` function.
- The error handling path has been modified: instead of jumping to `out_remove` when an error occurs while adding the IRQ chip, it now jumps to `out_pm_dis`.

### Relationships
The modification in the `gpio-tqmx86.c` file addresses a bug related to the unnecessary removal of the GPIO chip that was added using `devm_gpiochip_add_data()`. By removing the call to `gpiochip_remove`, the patch ensures that the GPIO chip is not incorrectly removed during error handling, which improves the stability of the GPIO probing process. The change in error handling flow reflects this correction, directing the flow to disable power management instead of attempting to remove the GPIO chip.

        Root cause:
        The bug was caused by an unnecessary call to `gpiochip_remove(&gpio->chip);` in the error handling path of the `tqmx86_gpio_probe` function. This function is responsible for adding a GPIO chip using `devm_gpiochip_add_data()`, which manages the GPIO chip's lifecycle automatically. Therefore, explicitly removing the GPIO chip when an error occurs during IRQ chip addition is incorrect and can lead to instability.
